PullRequest.Title: sessions: Delete user-shared environments from Remotes
PullRequest.Body:

Fixes #343985.

## Changes

- Add a trash-icon Delete action after Rename on Environment rows, including offline environments. Delete acts immediately, with no confirmation dialog.
- Restrict the action and inventory operation to `user-local` registrations. Managed sandboxes and unknown environment kinds are excluded.
- Call `DELETE /agents/environments/{id}` using the selected account's credential. Successful deletion (or an already absent record) invalidates discovery caches, persists inventory removal, cancels pending connections, and withdraws the local connection/provider. Errors retain the row and are reported to the user.
- Preserve keyboard navigation and restore table focus after deletion; prevent duplicate row actions while deletion is pending.
- Update accessibility help and add light/dark/high-contrast fixtures and regression tests.

Deleting a user-local environment removes its registration, not the machine or its local files. It is not a session-history erasure operation. The owning application can register a new environment afterward.

This branch starts from `origin/main` at `86db3b69224`; it is not stacked on an open PR.

## Validation

Passed:

```powershell
npm run build-fast -- --client-only
npm run typecheck-client
.\scripts\test.bat --run src\vs\sessions\contrib\providers\remoteAgentHost\test\browser\remotesModel.test.ts --run src\vs\sessions\contrib\providers\remoteAgentHost\test\browser\remotesWidget.test.ts --run src\vs\workbench\contrib\chat\test\browser\remoteAgentHost\missionControlEnvironmentService.test.ts --run src\vs\workbench\contrib\chat\test\browser\remoteAgentHost\cloudSandboxApiService.test.ts --reporter dot
npm run test-browser-no-install -- --browser webkit --browser chromium-msedge --run src\vs\sessions\contrib\providers\remoteAgentHost\test\browser\remotesWidget.test.ts --run src\vs\sessions\contrib\providers\remoteAgentHost\test\browser\remotesModel.test.ts --run src\vs\workbench\contrib\chat\test\browser\remoteAgentHost\missionControlEnvironmentService.test.ts --run src\vs\workbench\contrib\chat\test\browser\remoteAgentHost\cloudSandboxApiService.test.ts --reporter dot
```

- Electron: **625 passing**.
- Edge/WebKit: **1,247 passing** combined.
- Changed-TypeScript ESLint and direct hygiene: **14 files passed** each (`npm run eslint -- <changed TypeScript files>` and `node build\hygiene.ts <changed TypeScript files>`).
- `git diff --check`: **passed**.
- Component Explorer: inspected EnvironmentActions in dark, light, dark high contrast, and light high contrast; dark high-contrast stability check passed.
- Isolated Edge keyboard check: select the offline row, Tab to Rename, Right Arrow to Delete, Enter. The row disappeared without a dialog, the other environment remained, and focus returned to the table.

Tests cover 204/404 responses, HTTP failures, account-bound credentials, late completion after an account switch, stale discovery, persistence, pending connection cancellation, unsupported kinds, offline deletion, duplicate actions, and focus restoration.

No real environment was deleted during validation. Live backend deployment/proxy behavior and live host re-registration were not exercised.

## Manual test

1. Open **Manage Remote Environments** with GitHub Environments enabled and available.
2. Hover or focus a disposable user-shared Environment row and activate Delete after Rename.
3. Verify there is no confirmation; the row disappears after success. Check both online and offline rows, and confirm SSH/WSL/Tunnel rows do not gain Delete.
4. Refresh or reopen the editor and verify the deleted registration remains absent unless its owning application has registered again.
5. With a failing request, verify the row stays, an error is reported, and Delete can be retried.

Findings.ConfidenceRationale: The shared counter, the exact post-scan mismatch branch, the scan's network cardinality/concurrency, and the caller's retry backoff are all directly traced in production code. Magnitude varies with task count and whether deletion overlaps a scan, but the mechanism and critical-path delay are deterministic when it does.
Findings.PerformanceResource: Paginated task-list requests plus per-task detail, repository, and history network requests from an in-flight sandbox session discovery scan
Findings.PerformanceScaling: On a cold/full scan, discarded work grows with the number of task pages across the four repository/archive lanes and with the number of sandbox tasks requiring detail reads (bounded to five concurrent detail requests); warm scans still repeat the fixed list fan-out plus changed-task reads.
Findings.PerformanceOutcome: Wasted network I/O and delayed sandbox-session discovery; the failed result backs off the next poll from 60 seconds to 2 minutes, or effectively up to the 5-minute safety interval when the session feed is connected.
Findings.PreviousBehavior: Before this PR, environment registrations could not be deleted here, so an environment-only operation did not advance the generation used by sandbox task discovery. Existing generation bumps were tied to authentication or task/history mutations that actually affect that discovery cache.
Findings.ChangedBehavior: A successful environment DELETE now increments `_discoveryGeneration`, the same counter captured by `listSessions`; an unrelated task scan that finishes afterward returns `kind: 'failed'` instead of publishing or caching its completed result.
Findings.CausalDiffEvidence: The added line `this._discoveryGeneration++;` immediately after successful environment deletion is the only new operation that changes the generation observed by the independent `listSessions` pipeline.
Findings.Title: Keep environment invalidation out of sandbox task discovery
Findings.Impact: Deleting a user-shared environment while startup or periodic sandbox discovery is in flight can throw away a potentially large completed scan, force the same task inventory/details to be fetched again, and leave cloud sessions stale or absent until the backed-off retry.
Findings.Evidence: `listSessions` captures `_discoveryGeneration` at cloudSandboxApiService.ts:592, performs four paginated task-list lanes and up to one detail read per uncached/changed sandbox task with concurrency 5, then at lines 833-835 converts any generation mismatch into a failed result before committing the cache. `CloudSandboxSessionContribution` treats that result as a discovery failure and doubles its 60-second retry interval (lines 428-431); with a connected feed, `_refreshIfStale` uses at least the 5-minute safety interval (lines 301-304). Environment deletion does not alter task/session data, so the added increment is unrelated to all of that work.
Findings.Recommendation: Use a separate environment-inventory generation for `getCachedEnvironments`/`listEnvironments`, and advance only that generation here (while still clearing `_environments`) so stale environment reads are rejected without invalidating sandbox task discovery.

Scenarios.Scenario: Open or update Manage Remote Environments and render the new Delete row action
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Reading the observable remote inventory, rebuilding grouped rows, splicing the table, and laying it out are synchronous on the visible UI path. The diff adds one Action object to each instantiated actions-column template and includes it only for removable environment rows; no external boundary is reached.
Scenarios.ScalingInput: Number of currently rendered/visible table row templates and total remote rows processed by the existing full render; table virtualization bounds instantiated DOM/action templates to the viewport.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Single renderer/UI thread; observable updates may trigger renders, but the added action does not schedule independent work until activated.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: The widget consumes the model's existing observable inventory and table identity provider. No new cache, cache miss, or discovery call is introduced by merely rendering the action.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: the complete renderer and widget render path were inspected, including full-table splice/layout behavior.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: The modal can contain many remotes, but the incremental allocation is one small Action per visible template and does not establish a reportable rendering regression.
Scenarios.Verdict: No finding. The additional row action is bounded by visible table templates and adds no boundary or meaningful scaling mechanism.

Scenarios.Scenario: Confirm and successfully delete one online or offline user-local environment
Scenarios.CriticalPath: After user confirmation, completion waits for authentication resolution, one HTTP DELETE (up to the existing 10-second request timeout), a second account check, host filtering, and synchronous storage submission. UI row removal follows the observable host update. Connection withdrawal is launched by `_replaceHosts` but is intentionally fire-and-forget and therefore off the deletion critical path.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Resolve the selected GitHub authentication session through the registered authentication provider before DELETE and again after the response for account validation; exact-scope lookup is two calls total, with a fallback all-session lookup possible for each miss.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Normally two provider `getSessions` calls per deletion; up to four if exact-scope lookup misses and fallback enumeration runs.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: No environment deletion workflow existed, so these authentication lookups were absent from this action.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Both resolutions must finish before the delete workflow returns and the row is committed as removed.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: DELETE `/agents/environments/{id}` with the selected account credential.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Exactly one request per confirmed attempt; no automatic retry for DELETE.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The UI and inventory service exposed no environment deletion request.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: The backend response is the dominant required boundary before local inventory removal.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Submit all remaining environment metadata entries plus removed keys through profile storage `storeAll`.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One storage batch per successful deletion containing O(H) remaining hosts plus stale metadata removals.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: This persistence routine already ran on inventory refresh/status changes, but deletion newly invokes it once for this user action.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Synchronous submission occurs before deletion resolves, although durable flushing may be deferred by the storage implementation.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Dispose/remove the local remote-agent-host connection for the deleted environment, closing any live client transport.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: At most one connection removal for the deleted host.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: No deletion path withdrew an environment connection; existing inventory withdrawal used the same cleanup.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Launched without awaiting it, so cleanup is off the delete/UI critical path.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: One selected environment per action; local filtering and persistence scale with the account's environment inventory H. Per-row pending state prevents duplicate actions for the same environment, while separate user-confirmed rows can proceed independently.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Duplicate deletion of the same row is suppressed. Different rows have no shared limiter, but each requires explicit modal confirmation, so realistic aggregate concurrency is user-bounded. Disconnect cleanup is asynchronous and one call per removed host.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: The warm environment cache is cleared and in-flight environment reads are invalidated after success; a later refresh is cold. There is no automatic negative cache for deletion, but 404 is treated as success. The same invalidation counter is incorrectly shared with sandbox task discovery, which produced the submitted finding.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: the full call chain, timeout, provider dispatch, storage batch, and asynchronous connection removal were inspected.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Authentication-provider and storage latency are platform-dependent, but each is low-cardinality. Inventory size is normally modest. These costs do not independently justify another finding.
Scenarios.Verdict: One reportable issue exists only in the collateral shared-generation invalidation; the intended one-request deletion, local persistence, and one-host cleanup are bounded.

Scenarios.Scenario: Delete an environment while cold or periodic cloud-sandbox session discovery is in flight
Scenarios.CriticalPath: The DELETE is independent of task discovery, but its new generation increment causes `listSessions` to return a failed result after all scan work completes and before publishing/caching it. The session contribution then retains stale session state and waits for a later poll; failure doubles the retry interval from 60 to 120 seconds, and a connected feed imposes a five-minute minimum safety interval.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: List task inventory across active/archived and with/without-repository lanes, with pagination.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: At least four list requests on a full pass, plus one request for every additional 100-task page in each lane; an incremental pass still has the four logical lanes.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: One completed scan could publish/cache its result unless authentication or task/history state actually changed; environment-only actions did not invalidate it.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: All responses must be processed before discovery reaches the generation check; the new environment-only increment then discards them, delaying session publication until retry.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Fetch task details and, when needed, repository names or persisted histories.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Up to one detail request per uncached/changed sandbox task, with optional repository/history requests; detail concurrency is five.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The calls belonged to one discovery pass and their results were committed when that pass completed; environment deletion could not force a replay.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: These calls are part of the discarded scan and may be repeated because the pass cannot commit its local cache/checkpoint.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Cold/full discovery scans four repository/archive categories with pagination at 100 tasks per page, then performs detail reads for uncached or changed sandbox tasks and optional repository/history reads. Effective detail concurrency is capped at five, but total call count scales with task pages and qualifying tasks.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Inventory scans are serialized by the contribution. Per-task details run through a shared limiter of five. The diff does not increase simultaneous detail concurrency; it discards the completed pass and causes a later serialized replay.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Warm `_discoveredTasks` state survives, but the invalidated pass cannot commit newly fetched cache entries or its discovery checkpoint. The next pass therefore repeats list fan-out and may repeat the same detail/repository/history misses. Environment and task discovery should have separate generations.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: Very high: shared counter writes/reads, request cardinality, limiter, pre-commit generation check, and caller retry policy are explicit in production code.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Overlap timing and account task count vary, affecting wasted bytes and duration, but startup/periodic scans and user-triggered deletion can realistically overlap. The deterministic failed-result/backoff path establishes impact even without exact latency measurements.
Scenarios.Verdict: Reportable medium-severity repeated network work and delayed session discovery. A finding was submitted on the added shared-generation increment.

Scenarios.Scenario: Environment deletion fails, is cancelled, or receives 404
Scenarios.CriticalPath: A non-404 HTTP failure ends after the request/status handling and leaves inventory, cache, storage, and connection unchanged; the widget re-renders to re-enable the action. Cancellation likewise avoids commit. A 404 follows the successful path because absence is authoritative.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Attempt the environment DELETE and read status/error response.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: The failure response gates UI error reporting and action re-enablement.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: One request per explicit attempt; retries require another user activation. Error rendering scales with the existing table rows but occurs once per attempt.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Same-row duplicate actions remain suppressed for the full promise lifetime. There is no automatic retry burst or queued replay.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Non-404 failures preserve the warm environment cache and inventory. 404 clears the cache like 2xx because the record is already absent. No failure is negatively cached, but retries are manual rather than event-driven.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: status branches and widget pending-action lifetime are directly covered by changed production code.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Users can manually retry persistent failures, but there is no automatic frequency amplifier.
Scenarios.Verdict: No additional finding. Failure preserves caches/state and requires explicit retry; 404 success intentionally converges local state.

Analysis.Summary: Completed the performance pass over all 15 changed files and traced UI rendering, confirmation, authentication, DELETE, cache invalidation, persistence, connection cleanup, and sandbox discovery retry behavior. Submitted one medium finding for environment deletion invalidating and replaying unrelated sandbox task discovery; other changed costs are low-cardinality or off the critical path.
